titulek: Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
titulekPuvodni: Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
shrnuti: Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.

vyrez.text:
Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports — Meduza
Skip to main content
Russia planned ‘false flag’ operation with mass casualties on Polish territory, Rzeczpospolita reports
November 18, 2026, 9:26 am
Source: Rzeczpospolita
Russian intelligence services planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory for late October or early November, senior sources told the Polish newspaper Rzeczpospolita. The plan could have involved crossing the border and staging an attack on a target inside Poland.
They said the sabotage could have been staged as a “false flag” operation meant to pin the blame on Kyiv.
The warning about the planned sabotage came from intelligence services in partner countries, though analysts at Polish intelligence agencies also raised the possibility of a provocation, the newspaper’s sources said. Rzeczpospolita reported that similar warnings were sent to intelligence services in the Baltic states: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania.
“We had information about specific sites where the attack was supposed to take place. The Russians were counting on a large number of casualties,” one of the newspaper’s sources…

Velení polských bezpečnostních sil vyslalo do Podlaského a Varmijsko-mazurského vojvodství posily, včetně příslušníků polské speciální jednotky GROM, dalších příslušníků pohraniční stráže a policejních protiteroristických jednotek.
Podle polského premiéra Donalda Tuska se posily aktivovaly, když pohraničníci v noci na úterý zaznamenali…

No drone crashes were reported.

A destroyed residential building. Photo: Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration
Russian attacks killed at least 372 civilians in Ukraine in October 2026, while another 1,981 people were injured. This was the highest civilian death toll for October since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion and 95% higher than in October 2025, when 183 people were killed and 1,021 injured.
Source: a report by the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU)
Details: Russia's long-range weapons remained the leading cause of deaths and injuries. Missile and drone strikes accounted for 55% of all casualties, namely 177 people killed and 1,108 injured.

Russia’s government has submitted a bill to the State Duma that would establish special bankruptcy procedures for war participants: mobilized soldiers and those who have signed military contracts.
Under the bill, if an arbitration court grants a bankruptcy petition, property worth up to 10 million rubles would be excluded from the “bankruptcy estate” (all of a debtor’s assets subject to sale to repay creditors). The court would decide which property qualifies.
The bill’s explanatory note states that the legislation “has a high social orientation, reflected in the implementation of special support measures” for Russians who have signed military service contracts.
“An analysis of court practice shows it would be worthwhile to codify the proposed approaches,” the bill’s authors added.

Estonian public media ERR News has an interesting interview with the country's security service chief concerning a recent incident in which eight Latvian nationals were arrested on suspicion of a Russia-backed sabotage plot.
In the interview Estonian Internal Security Service (ISS/KAPO) Director General Margo Palloson acknowledges the assistance received from his Latvian counterparts in foiling the plot and also considers the wider implications – which may include the complete closure of Estonia's border with Russia.
That in turn could make it advisable for Latvia to follow suit, it is intimated.

Na pražské Letné se podle organizátorů sešlo zhruba 400 tisíc lidí, což by z nedělní demonstrace Milionu chvilek udělalo největší protestní akci od roku 1989. Mikuláš Minář zde představil požadavky protestujících na vládu a premiéra Andreje Babiše.

Premiér Andrej Babiš v reakci na demonstraci řekl , že mediální poplatky vláda zruší, protože kabinet plní svůj program.
Na Letné protestovali senioři, rodiny s dětmi i studenti. „Jsme teprve v prváku, ale víme, o co jde, a chceme to podpořit,“ říká jedna ze středoškolaček.

TALLINN — Imagine French General Charles de Gaulle, exiled in London during World War II, running his Free France government by logging into the cloud.
Officials in Estonia are preparing for exactly such a scenario with a new strategy to boost doomsday resilience — hukukindlus in Estonian — that would allow the government’s digital services to be run entirely from abroad if its territory is occupied by a foreign enemy.
The Baltic country of 1.3 million, which shares a 294-kilometer border with Russia, fears it is a prime target if Moscow were to invade a European Union country. Security services have already warned that Russia is waging a hybrid war on Europe, and Estonia has blamed Moscow for everything from cyberattacks to arson plots to cuts to undersea data cables .

Estland sluit per 1 december de grensovergangen met Rusland. Aanleiding is een vermoedelijke sabotageactie tegen een Ests defensiebedrijf. Tallinn houdt Moskou daarvoor verantwoordelijk.
Acht personen met de Letse nationaliteit zijn aangehouden op verdenking van een poging tot brandstichting. Dat gebeurde afgelopen nacht bij Threod Systems, een fabrikant van drones in Viimsi, ten noorden van de hoofdstad Tallinn. Volgens de Estse autoriteiten is de opdracht voor de sabotageactie gegeven door GRU, de Russische militaire inlichtingendienst.

Estland heeft beslist om alle grensovergangen met buurland Rusland te sluiten na een nieuwe poging tot brandstichting bij een wapenfabrikant die drones levert aan Oekraïne. Volgens de regering in Tallinn zit de Russische inlichtingendienst GRU achter de sabotageactie.

Gisterenochtend was er een poging tot brandstichting bij de Estse dronesfabrikant Threod Systems, die onder meer aan Oekraïne levert. De materiële schade bleef beperkt doordat het beveiligingspersoneel van het bedrijf snel kon ingrijpen. Intussen zijn 8 verdachten opgepakt.

The foiled attack happened in Viimsi, north of the capital, Tallinn.

Eight Latvian nationals have been detained after an attempt to commit arson at Estonian drone manufacturer Threod Systems, reports Estonian public media ERR .
Estonia's domestic intellegence service has attributed the arson plot to Russia's military intelligence agency, the GRU. Estonia is planning to close its eastern border in response.
Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said at a press conference on Sunday that there was an attempt to break into Threod Systems' property in Viimsi, near Tallinn, to start a fire at 3.06 a.m. on Saturday, November 14th.
The incident was thwarted thanks to the intervention of Threod's security team, Asi added.

De problemen doken maandag op rond 18 uur en duurden ongeveer 20 minuten. Russia attacks Ukraine with 132 drones overnight, 78 of them jet-powered | Ukrainska Pravda
A mobile fire group. Stock photo: General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine
Russia attacked Ukraine with 132 drones on the night of 14-15 November. Ukrainian air defence downed 106 Russian UAVs.
Source: Ukraine's Air Force
Quote: "On the night of 14-15 November (from 18:00 on 14 November), the enemy attacked with 132 attack UAVs, including with Shahed (78 jet-powered) and Gerbera attack drones and Parodiya decoy drones, launched from the directions of Bryansk, Oryol, Kursk, Millerovo and Primorsko-Akhtarsk in Russia, as well as temporarily occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske in temporarily occupied Crimea."
Advertisement:





Details: Early reports indicate that as of 08:00, air defence had shot down or jammed 106 Russian Shahed-type UAVs (61 of them jet-powered), Gerbera drones and other types of drones.
Hits by Russian drones were recorded at 20 locations.

shrnuti: A large-scale drone attack on Nizhnekamsk caused a major fire at Nizhnekamskneftekhim, one of Europe's largest petrochemical plants, eyewitness footage shows.

Drones spark major fire at petrochemical plant in Tatarstan | Ukrainska Pravda
The plant following the drone attack. Photo: Supernova+
The city of Nizhnekamsk in Russia's Republic of Tatarstan, the country's largest centre for petrochemical production , came under a large-scale drone attack on the night of 14-15 November. A major fire broke out at the Nizhnekamskneftekhim plant.
Source: Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channels Exilenova+ , Supernova+ and Falcon Insight Map ; Russian media outlet Astra
Advertisement:





Quote from Astra : "Footage filmed by eyewitnesses shows a major fire following the strike... Nizhnekamskneftekhim PJSC (NKNK) is one of the largest petrochemical complexes in Europe. The plant is part of the Sibur holding company... and produces synthetic rubber, plastics and ethylene."



The plant following the drone attack.



Photo: Exilenova+



Details: The industrial zone of Nizhnekamsk, where the facility is located, as well as the Tatneft oil refinery, have been attacked several times.

shrnuti: Russian guided aerial bombs struck Zaporizhzhia on 14 November, damaging apartment blocks and dozens of cars, causing a fire and injuring six people, including a two-year-old child.

Russian aerial bombs hit Zaporizhzhia apartment blocks, injuring six, including child | Ukrainska Pravda
The aftermath of the Russian attack. Photo: Zaporizhzhia Oblast Defence Council
Russian guided aerial bombs damaged several apartment blocks and dozens of cars in Zaporizhzhia on the evening of 14 November. A fire broke out in one of the buildings, and six people, including a child, were injured.
Source: Mykhailo Semikin , acting head of Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration; Ivan Fedorov , co-chair of Zaporizhzhia Oblast Defence Council



A firefighter



Photo: Zaporizhzhia City Council


Advertisement:






Quote from Semikin: "The enemy has launched eight strikes on Zaporizhzhia. The attack has damaged the windows of an apartment block and parked cars. A fire has broken out at the site of the strike. Early reports indicate that five people have been injured."



The aftermath of the Russian attack



Photo: Zaporizhzhia Oblast Military Administration



Details: Russia launched at least eight guided aerial bombs in the attack on the city. Windows were shattered in several apartment blocks. Dozens of cars were damaged.

Scheduled electricity outages will be in effect around the clock in some regions of Ukraine on Sunday, November 15.
According to Ukrinform, the national energy company Ukrenergo announced this on Facebook .


The company said that hourly power outage schedules would apply to all categories of consumers throughout the day. The restrictions will range from one to two outage groups.


Power consumption restrictions will also be imposed on industrial consumers.
